## Human review verdict — web-everything/web-everything#1561

**Verdict:** ✅ pass — no blocking findings

### Panel verdicts

| lens | weight | verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| correctness | mandatory | accept |

### Findings (1)

**unverified-guarantee** (1)
- `scripts/operations/__tests__/helpers/fake-claude.mjs:88` — The `if (bg) {...}` branch and its non-bg fallthrough are timing-identical (both write state and exit(0) immediately, no delay anywhere in the shim), so the test asserting `--bg` "returns instead of blocking" can never go red for the property its comment claims to prove. — Ran the shim standalone with and without `--bg`: with `--bg` it returned in 257ms, without it returned in 48ms — both trivially under the test's 10s bound, because neither code path in the fake simulates the real CLI's actual background-fork-vs-wait semantics (that distinction lives entirely in the external `claude` binary, outside this repo). Mutation check: there is no line in this diff or in dispatch-lane-io.mjs whose removal would turn this specific assertion red — it is permanently green by construction. The narrower, real regression it might guard against (`--bg` dropped from the argv) is already independently caught by case 1's `expect(seen).toContain('--bg')`, so no named test reddens for the property this test's own docstring claims ("the property the whole dispatch model rests on"), but the practical blast radius is small since case 1 covers the argv-presence risk. _[impact if unfixed: cosmetic]_
  - _Prevention (OWED — file it):_ Extend the PR's own 'mutation-checked, both ways' practice to every case, including this one: before trusting a 'proves X' test, delete/invert the thing X depends on and confirm the named test reddens. This is a judgment call, not something a deterministic lint can enforce, so file it as a test-authoring checklist item rather than a gate.

---

**Decision:** `changes` — recorded by operator.
**Lens:** `correctness` — a SINGLE-LENS run. One `judge` step, one juror, one lens; the table above lists only the lens that judged. The other 3 panel lenses (security, simplicity, standards-conformance) did NOT run and are not reported as unjudged.
Net basis: `e9aa38f6eacb7ed0341cdcb4a191c5f9e56f0b15..eaa1bc906bd2fc088789a2c9b87a54ac9d2faa33` (rev `origin/lane/test-harness-fake-claude` at review time) — 2 net changed file(s) vs current main (#2450), not `gh pr diff`'s three-dot list.

_Recorded through the declared `review-pr` operation (#3035)._

## Independent review — `review:changes`

Run `review-pr-baaeaa60-ac4d-4be0-a12b-7c0919dfe534`, lens `correctness`. Every citation below was opened;
every mutation below was actually run in a juror lane (lane-31) at `eaa1bc90` on `origin/main` `e9aa38f6`.

### Verified correct first, so the bounce is not read wider than it is

- All three quoted citations exist and are faithfully elided. `dispatch-lane-io.mjs:606-607` really does say
  *"untested against the real CLI, and a wrong bet turns into a dispatch with a mangled prompt"* (it spans a
  line break, which is why a naive grep misses it). `real-repo.mjs:14-16` matches verbatim.
- The gate reproduces exactly: **0 errors, 1435 warnings**, and I confirmed "unchanged from baseline" by
  running it again with the two files removed — also 1435.
- "99 passed" resolves: `dispatch-lane.test.mjs` (93) + this file (6). Six cases, 1.53s. Accurate.
- "The first test that starts a `claude` process" is accurate — `dispatch-crosses-processes.test.mjs`
  explicitly disclaims starting one.
- The fake genuinely wins `PATH` for the spawn seam; the shim's own stderr appears in the run.

The harness works. The findings are about claims the diff makes that do not hold.

---

### F1 — the docblocks this PR is built on now say something false, and the PR updates neither (high)

`dispatch-lane-io.mjs:528` still reads:

> NOT YET PROVEN LIVE. No test starts a `claude` process, and no dispatch has been fired end to end …

`dispatch-lane-integration.test.mjs:7` repeats it as current fact. After this lands, "No test starts a
`claude` process" is flatly false, and it is false *because of this PR*. The diff quotes those two lines
three times as its justification and touches neither file (2 files changed, both new).

The other two clauses survive but need qualifying: "no dispatch has been fired end to end" is still true, and
"the CLI's response to it is not [asserted]" is still true of the *real* CLI. So this is a rewrite, not a
deletion.

### F2 — the round-trip case does not use production's observer, and its comment says it does (high)

`dispatch-spawn-live.test.mjs:64-67` hand-rolls the read:

```js
// The observer's read, run as its own process exactly as production does it.
const listing = JSON.parse(execFileSync('claude', ['agents', '--json'], {
  encoding: 'utf8', env: { ...process.env, ...fake.env },
}));
```

Production is `defaultListAgents` (`dispatch-lane-io.mjs:876`, exported), and it is not that: it also passes
`stdio: ['ignore','pipe','pipe']`, `maxBuffer`, `timeout: listTimeoutMs(env)`, `killSignal: 'SIGKILL'`, and
its own `JSON.parse(String(out || '[]'))` empty-listing fallback. None of that is exercised.

This matters more than a wrong comment, because the reason it was hand-rolled is a real gap the PR does not
name: **`defaultListAgents` cannot be pointed at the fake at all.** Its `env` option feeds only
`listTimeoutMs(env)` and never reaches the child. I probed it:

```js
defaultListAgents({ env: { ...process.env, ...fake.env } })
```

returned this machine's **real** live sessions — including this very review session — and
`fake.calls().length` was **0**.

So the harness's `PATH` technique only works against seams that forward `env` to the child. `defaultSpawnAgent`
does (via `...opts`); `defaultListAgents` does not. Consequently PR claim #2 — the commit calls it *"the one
that matters most"*, *"both ends of that chain were previously modelled and nothing tied them together"* —
ties the dispatcher to a re-implementation of the observer, not to the observer. Either give
`defaultListAgents` an env passthrough and call it, or say plainly that the observer half is still uncovered.

### F3 — the mutation evidence is non-discriminating (medium)

> ## Mutation-checked, both ways … Neither test passes with the behaviour removed.

Both mutations do redden the claimed case — I ran them. But both also redden **pre-existing** tests, so
neither shows this file detects anything the suite did not already catch:

| mutation | new file | pre-existing |
|---|---|---|
| prompt moved to front of argv | case 1 | `dispatch-lane.test.mjs:646`, `:657`, `dispatch-lane-defaults` — **3 red** |
| leading-dash guard deleted | case 3 | `dispatch-lane.test.mjs:652` — **1 red** |
| (mine) binary renamed `claude`→`claude-cli` | 4 cases | `dispatch-lane-defaults` — **2 red** |

The section is presented as proof the file earns its keep; it proves the tests are *sensitive*, not that they
add coverage. I did not find a mutation only this file catches — I tried three. If one exists, it is the
evidence worth putting in the body.

### F4 — case 6 cannot fail for the reason it names (medium)

`` `--bg` returns instead of blocking `` asserts elapsed `< 10_000`. The shim has no blocking path in either
branch — no sleep, no env knob — so no change to production code or fixture config makes it exceed the bound.
Under my binary-rename mutation it failed only because the spawn threw. The property also already has a home:
`dispatch-lane-defaults.test.mjs`, *"the agent spawn is bounded — `claude --bg` returns immediately"*.
(The operation's own juror reached this independently.)

### F5 — case 4 asserts the fixture, and not in the shape it claims (medium)

> That refusal is **not decorative** — an unguarded dash really is parsed as an unknown flag and rejected.

The parser doing the rejecting is the 20-line shim added by this same diff (`fake-claude.mjs`,
`if (a.startsWith('-'))`). It is circular. Separately, the argv used is `'--not-a-real-flag'` — a token that
is unambiguously a flag. The hazard the guard exists for is a *brief* like `'--help me'`: one argv element
containing a space. The shim rejects that too, so the faithful demonstration was available and free.

### F6 — case 3's second assertion is vacuous (low)

`expect(fake.calls()).toHaveLength(0)` — the test body never spawns under any outcome (`buildAgentArgv` is
pure), so "BEFORE any process starts" holds regardless of the guard. The load-bearing half,
`.toThrow(/begins with/)`, duplicates `dispatch-lane.test.mjs:652`.

### F7 — dead surface in the fixture (low)

`withFakeClaude` returns `pathPrefix`, `dir` and `sessions()`; **no consumer anywhere in the repo** uses any
of the three (grepped repo-wide — the only importer is this test file, which uses `env`, `lastArgv`, `calls`,
`cleanup`). The shim's `if (a === '--') { … }` branch is unreachable: `buildAgentArgv` never emits `--` and no
test passes it — and it models precisely the thing `dispatch-lane-io.mjs:606` says it *declined* to bet on, so
it is a fidelity claim nothing checks.

### F8 — nothing enforces that the fake won `PATH` (low, forward-looking)

Every case passes `fake.env` today, so this is not a present bug. But the file is explicitly a harness meant
to be extended, and my F2 probe shows the failure mode is live: a call that omits (or structurally cannot
apply) the override silently reaches the real CLI on this machine. For a `--bg` argv that means launching a
real background agent, against a file whose headline promise is *"no model runs, no token is spent"*. A
sentinel the shim stamps and `spawnVia` checks would make that promise enforced rather than conventional.

---

**Not blocking, noted:** `fake-claude.mjs:5-8` attributes *"NOT YET PROVEN LIVE"* to
"`dispatch-lane-io.mjs`'s own integration test"; the line is the **sink's** own docblock, which
`dispatch-spawn-live.test.mjs:4-5` gets right. Worth making the two new files agree.

*Reviewed independently; the author's session did not record this verdict.*

## Human review verdict — web-everything/web-everything#1561

**Verdict:** ✅ pass — no blocking findings

### Panel verdicts

| lens | weight | verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| correctness | mandatory | accept |

### Findings (2)

**coverage** (1)
- `scripts/operations/__tests__/helpers/fake-claude.mjs:150` — `assertWins` is documented as an enforced safety guard against accidentally hitting the real `claude` CLI, but no test exercises the guard itself — every call site already passes a correctly-configured env, so the check is a no-op in the current suite. — If a future edit to `assertWins` (or to how `spawnVia`/callers build `env`) silently broke the check — e.g. comparing against the wrong path, or swallowing the resolution error — nothing in this file or its neighbour would catch it, because none of the five cases ever calls it with a mis-pointed PATH. Mutation check: deleting the `fake.assertWins(env);` line inside `spawnVia` (dispatch-spawn-live.test.mjs) does not redden any named test in this file — every case's env already has the fake winning PATH, so the assertion is never the thing standing between pass and fail. The guarantee ("Enforced rather than conventional") is stated but currently undefended by any test. _[CONFIRMED]_ _[impact if unfixed: degraded]_
  - _Prevention (OWED — file it):_ Add one small case asserting `assertWins` throws when pointed at an env that doesn't include the fake's directory (e.g. `assertWins(process.env)` when a real `claude` isn't on PATH, or a stubbed `command -v` returning a different path) — a cheap addition to the same file, not a new gate.

**test-flakiness** (1)
- `scripts/operations/__tests__/dispatch-spawn-live.test.mjs:128` — The `--bg` vs foreground timing case asserts an absolute wall-clock bound (`background < 1_000`) rather than a relative one, so it depends on this machine/CI being fast enough to spawn two node subprocesses well under a second. — Under CI contention (many parallel vitest workers each forking node child processes) a cold node start for the backgrounded call could plausibly exceed 1000ms even though `--bg` still returned immediately relative to the 1500ms foreground sleep, producing an intermittent false-red on an otherwise-correct dispatch. Not a mutation-catchable defect — this is about the test's own reliability, not a guarded line, so no mutation probe applies. _[PLAUSIBLE]_ _[impact if unfixed: degraded]_
  - _Prevention (OWED — file it):_ Prefer `expect(background).toBeLessThan(foreground / 2)` (or similar relative comparison) over an absolute ceiling whenever a test's real claim is comparative timing, not an absolute duration.

---

Net basis: `e9aa38f6eacb7ed0341cdcb4a191c5f9e56f0b15..1cd5c2b0ae077a6008946f7489011c2fa3c93ff2` (rev `origin/lane/test-harness-fake-claude` at review time) — 4 net changed file(s) vs current main (#2450), not `gh pr diff`'s three-dot list.

## Independent re-review — `review:changes`

Run `review-pr-a3fad700-e633-4cb1-bd6e-4e5db14d3411`, lens `correctness`, head `1cd5c2b0` on `origin/main`
`e9aa38f6`. Every count below was **run**, not read; every mutation was executed against the whole
`scripts/operations/__tests__/` suite in a lane at that head. The juror reduced to `accept` with two
carve-outs; the operator's own verification found three claim defects it did not check, so the verdict is
`changes`.

### Round 1's eight findings — disposition

| # | disposition | evidence |
|---|---|---|
| F1 docblocks now false | **addressed** | `dispatch-lane-io.mjs:528` now reads *"PROVEN AGAINST A PROCESS, NOT AGAINST THE REAL CLI … What is still NOT proven: no dispatch has been fired end to end, and the REAL CLI's response to this argv remains unasserted."* `dispatch-lane-integration.test.mjs:3-8` rewritten to point at the new file. Both surviving clauses kept and correctly qualified. |
| F2 observer hand-rolled | **addressed** | `dispatch-spawn-live.test.mjs:86` is now `defaultListAgents({ env })`; `dispatch-lane-io.mjs:891` adds the `env` passthrough. I re-probed the old failure mode by mutation — see below — and it is now caught. |
| F3 mutation evidence non-discriminating | **addressed** | The body now reports the three non-discriminating mutations honestly *and* adds one that only this file catches. I ran all four (details below). |
| F4 case 6 unfalsifiable | **addressed** | `FAKE_CLAUDE_WORK_MS` gives the shim a real 1.5s foreground path (`fake-claude.mjs:106-107`); the case now measures fg vs bg. Dropping `--bg` from `buildAgentArgv` would redden it. |
| F5 case 4 asserts the fixture | **addressed** | The hazard is now a real brief — `'--help me, my first heading starts with a dash'` (`:99`) — not `--not-a-real-flag`. The circularity is now stated outright in the file's own docblock (`:16-20`) rather than claimed away. |
| F6 vacuous assertion | **addressed** | `expect(fake.calls()).toHaveLength(0)` is gone; `:109` asserts the argv actually reached the parser. |
| F7 dead surface | **partly — see N3** | The `--` branch is gone (`fake-claude.mjs:75-77` says why). `pathPrefix`, `dir`, `sessions()` are gone. **`calls()` is not**, and the sentence written to close F7 now claims it is. |
| F8 nothing enforces PATH | **addressed** | `assertWins` (`fake-claude.mjs:152-157`) resolves `claude` the way the OS does (`sh -c 'command -v claude'`) rather than inspecting the `PATH` string, and `spawnVia` calls it first, every time. |

Non-blocking note from round 1 (the `fake-claude.mjs:5-8` misattribution) is also fixed — it now credits the
sink's own docblock.

### Verified correct

- **The mutation table is real.** Run across the whole `scripts/operations/__tests__/` suite (284 files), diffed
  against a baseline run of the same suite:
  - *delete `defaultListAgents`'s `env` passthrough* → **exactly one** new failure, `dispatch-spawn-live.test.mjs`
    case 2, `expected [ …(15) ] to include 'aaaaaaaa-bbbb-cccc-dddd-eeeeeeeeeeee'`. **Zero pre-existing.** The
    headline row holds — this file catches something nothing else does, and it exists because of the F2 fix.
  - *prompt to front of argv* → case 1 + **3 pre-existing** (`dispatch-lane.test.mjs` ×2, `dispatch-lane-defaults` ×1). Matches.
  - *leading-dash guard deleted* → case 3 + **1 pre-existing** (`dispatch-lane.test.mjs`). Matches.
  - *binary renamed* → see N2.
- **`npm run check:standards`: 0 errors, 1435 warnings.** Reproduced exactly.
- Both quoted citations are verbatim and faithfully elided: `real-repo.mjs:14-16` and
  `dispatch-lane-io.mjs:609-611` (the latter spans a line break).
- *"The first test that starts a `claude` process"* still holds — `dispatch-spawn-live.test.mjs` is the only
  file in `scripts/operations/__tests__/` that names the binary as a spawn target.
- CI is green on all four shards, so nothing here is a suite-red claim.

---

### F1 (new) — the gate line says **99 passed**; it is **98** (blocking)

> `npx vitest run` on the new file plus its neighbour: **99 passed**.

Run at `1cd5c2b0`:

```
✓ scripts/operations/__tests__/dispatch-lane.test.mjs  (93 tests)
✓ scripts/operations/__tests__/dispatch-spawn-live.test.mjs  (5 tests)
Tests  98 passed (98)
```

99 was correct **last round**, when the file had six cases (93 + 6). This round dropped it to five — the F6 fix —
and the number was not re-run. No pairing of this file with a neighbour yields 99: with
`dispatch-lane-integration` it is 9, with `dispatch-lane-defaults` 28, with `dispatch-lane` 98.

This is the same class the last three rounds died on, and it is *introduced by the fix* — a stale number left
behind by an otherwise-correct change, in a body whose own section heading is "Mutation-checked — and reported
honestly".

### F2 (new) — "Case 6" does not exist (blocking, same cause)

> Case 6 is also falsifiable for the first time.

The body's own list says **"Five cases"** and enumerates 1–5; the file has five `it()` blocks. "Case 6" is the
round-1 numbering, left un-renumbered by the same edit that removed a case. The paragraph is about what is now
case 5, and everything it says about it is true — only the label is wrong.

### F3 (new) — F7's fix introduces a new false statement (blocking; the "wrongly addressed" one)

`fake-claude.mjs:115-117`:

> The returned surface is exactly what a consumer uses and no more — an earlier cut also handed back
> `pathPrefix`, `dir` and `sessions()`, none of which anything imported.

Three members were removed and a fourth was left. Repo-wide, the only importer of this fixture is
`dispatch-spawn-live.test.mjs`, and it touches exactly four members:

```
fake.assertWins   fake.cleanup   fake.env   fake.lastArgv
```

`calls` (`fake-claude.mjs:142`) has **no consumer anywhere** — it is also still in the `@returns` type. So the
sentence written to certify that F7 was closed is itself an instance of F7. Either drop `calls` (`lastArgv`
already reads the same log) or drop the "and no more".

---

### N1 — `assertWins` is undefended by any test (non-blocking; juror CONFIRMED)

Every one of the five cases passes an env in which the fake already wins, so deleting `fake.assertWins(env)`
from `spawnVia` reddens nothing. The guard's docblock calls it *"Enforced rather than conventional"*; today the
enforcement is itself only conventional. One case asserting it throws against an env without the fake's dir
would close that, cheaply, in the same file.

### N2 — the mutation table's last row is seam-dependent (non-blocking)

> binary renamed `claude` → `claude-cli` | 4 cases | `dispatch-lane-defaults` — 2 red

Renaming **`defaultSpawnAgent`'s** binary alone reproduces that exactly: 4 cases here, 2 in
`dispatch-lane-defaults`. Renaming **both** seams — the plain reading of "the binary" now that
`defaultListAgents` is in scope — gives **6** in `dispatch-lane-defaults` and **5** in `wake-cli`. The row's
conclusion (non-discriminating) survives either way; it just needs to say which seam it renamed.

### N3 — `background < 1_000` is an absolute bound on a relative property (non-blocking; juror PLAUSIBLE)

`dispatch-spawn-live.test.mjs:134`. The claim is comparative — bg returns while fg blocks — but the assertion is
a fixed ceiling on a node cold start. Measured here in a full-suite run, case 5 took 2.3s wall against a 1.5s
foreground sleep, i.e. the backgrounded spawn landed around 0.8s: inside the bound, with roughly 20% of margin.
`expect(background).toBeLessThan(foreground / 2)` states the actual property and cannot flake on a slow box.
(Same run, on this contended laptop, case 1 hit production's 60s `SPAWN_TIMEOUT_MS` — but `wake-cli.test.mjs`
does the same thing on unmodified `main`, so that one is the machine, not this PR. CI is green. Recording it
only because it is the same fragility N3 names.)

---

### Prevention

Round 1's juror marked its prevention **OWED — file it** ("before trusting a 'proves X' test, delete/invert the
thing X depends on and confirm the named test reddens"). Nothing matching it is in `backlog/` — grep for
`mutation-checked` returns no item. That one is now discharged *in this diff*, but the prevention F1–F3 actually
need is narrower and is not filed either: **when an edit changes the case count, re-run the gate line rather than
carrying it forward.** Both new blocking findings and the F7 regression are the same act — a claim inherited
across a revision instead of re-derived from it.

*Reviewed independently; the author's session did not record this verdict. Juror spend: $0.51.*

## Human review verdict — web-everything/web-everything#1561

**Verdict:** 🔁 changes requested

### Panel verdicts

| lens | weight | verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| correctness | mandatory | changes |

### Findings (1)

**test-reliability** (1)
- `scripts/operations/__tests__/helpers/fake-claude.mjs:154` — `assertWins` only recognizes "claude resolves to a different binary than the fake"; it has no handling for "claude resolves to nothing at all," which is exactly the state of this repo's real CI. — `assertWins` calls `execFileSync('sh', ['-c', 'command -v claude'], { env })` and only afterward checks `if (resolved !== bin) throw new Error('...did not win PATH...')`. When the given `env`'s PATH has no `claude` anywhere on it, `command -v claude` itself exits non-zero and `execFileSync` throws BEFORE that check ever runs — with `Command failed: sh -c command -v claude`, not the guard's message. I reconstructed the exact file from the diff and ran it directly: `fake.assertWins({ PATH: '/usr/bin:/bin' })` throws `"Command failed: sh -c command -v claude"`, and `/did not win PATH/.test(e.message)` is `false`. `.github/workflows/ci.yml`'s `test`/`test-shard` jobs only run `npm ci` — there is no `@anthropic-ai/claude-code` global install anywhere in the workflow files (grepped, zero hits) — so on the project's actual CI runner, `claude` is not on PATH at all. That means the two assertions in `dispatch-spawn-live.test.mjs`'s "refuses to spawn when the fake did NOT win PATH" test — `expect(() => fake.assertWins({ ...process.env })).toThrow(/did not win PATH/)` and `expect(() => spawnVia(fake, argv, { PATH: process.env.PATH })).toThrow(/did not win PATH/)` — will fail on CI with a wrong-error mismatch, even though the guard's underlying intent (refuse when the fake doesn't win) is sound. The PR's own "Gate: 99 passed" was run on a machine (mirroring this dev box, where `claude` is npm-installed globally) that happens to have a real `claude` elsewhere on PATH, masking the gap. _[CONFIRMED]_ _[impact if unfixed: broken]_
  - _Prevention (OWED — file it):_ Have `assertWins` catch the `execFileSync` throw and normalize a not-found resolution to its own message (e.g. `resolved = safeResolve(env) ?? ''`) so the guard's behavior doesn't depend on whether some unrelated `claude` binary happens to exist on the host; short of that, this class of drift would be caught by a standing rule that a new subprocess-resolution test must be run once against a PATH stripped of ambient dev tools before merging.

---

**Decision:** `changes` — recorded by operator.
**Lens:** `correctness` — a SINGLE-LENS run. One `judge` step, one juror, one lens; the table above lists only the lens that judged. The other 3 panel lenses (security, simplicity, standards-conformance) did NOT run and are not reported as unjudged.
Net basis: `e9aa38f6eacb7ed0341cdcb4a191c5f9e56f0b15..95572d0c94b439f9b10e32c33333eb8c7a6aeb8b` (rev `origin/lane/test-harness-fake-claude` at review time) — 4 net changed file(s) vs current main (#2450), not `gh pr diff`'s three-dot list.

## Independent re-review — `review:changes`

Run `review-pr-6f3d0a11-728a-4bbf-b256-e43ca209ed5f`, lens `correctness` (single-lens, not a panel), head
`95572d0c` on `origin/main` `e7ab2833`. Every count below was **run** in a lane at that head; every citation
was opened. `scripts/operations/` is byte-identical between the PR's base `e9aa38f6` and current `main`, so
measurements transfer.

**The short version: CI is RED at this head, and the failure is the fix for round 2's N1.**

### Round 2's findings — disposition

| # | disposition | evidence |
|---|---|---|
| F1 `99 passed` was `98` | **addressed** | Re-ran the exact gate pair: `✓ dispatch-lane.test.mjs (93 tests)` + `✓ dispatch-spawn-live.test.mjs (6 tests)` → `Tests 99 passed (99)`. The number is right again, and right *because* a case was added, not because the old one was. **But see F1 (new): that run only passes on a host with a real `claude` installed.** |
| F2 "Case 6" did not exist | **addressed** | The file now has six `it()` blocks (`:52, :70, :94, :112, :118, :147`); the body says "Six cases" and enumerates 1–6, with item 6 = the new PATH-guard case. Renumbering matches. |
| F3 `calls()` + "and no more" | **addressed** | `calls` is gone from the returned object and from the `@returns` block. Repo-wide the only importer is `dispatch-spawn-live.test.mjs`, and it touches exactly `fake.env`, `fake.lastArgv`, `fake.assertWins`, `fake.cleanup` — all four surviving members. ### F1 (new, blocking) — the new PATH-guard case fails on CI, and the whole `test` check is red

`.github/workflows` never installs `@anthropic-ai/claude-code` (grepped: zero hits; the shards run `npm ci`
only). So on the runner, `claude` resolves to **nothing**. `fake-claude.mjs:154-158`:

```js
const resolved = execFileSync('sh', ['-c', 'command -v claude'], { encoding: 'utf8', env }).trim();
if (resolved !== bin) { throw new Error(`fake-claude: the fake did not win PATH — …`); }
```

`command -v` **exits non-zero when nothing is found**, so `execFileSync` throws before the comparison is ever
reached — with `Command failed: sh -c command -v claude`, not the guard's message. Probed directly at this
head:

```
fake.assertWins({ PATH: '/usr/bin:/bin' })
  → THREW: "Command failed: sh -c command -v claude"
  → /did not win PATH/ matches?  false
```

That is not a hypothetical. Run `32912897829` at `95572d0c`, `test-shard (1)`:

```
FAIL scripts/operations/__tests__/dispatch-spawn-live.test.mjs > … >
     refuses to spawn when the fake did NOT win PATH, rather than reaching the real CLI
AssertionError: expected [Function] to throw error matching /did not win PATH/
                but got 'Command failed: sh -c command -v clau…'
 ❯ scripts/operations/__tests__/dispatch-spawn-live.test.mjs:151:55
Tests  1 failed | 2077 passed | 1 skipped (2079)
```

`test` → **fail**. `test-shard (1)` → **fail**. The two prior heads (`eaa1bc90`, `1cd5c2b0`) were both green;
this round turned CI red.

Three things make this the round's central finding rather than a stray flake:

1. **It is the fix for N1.** Round 2 said the guard was decorative. The case written to make it load-bearing
   asserts a message the guard only emits when *some unrelated `claude` binary happens to exist elsewhere on
   the host* — so the test passes on the author's box and fails everywhere the guard actually matters.
2. **The guard already knows about this branch and cannot reach it.** Its message interpolates
   `${resolved || '(nothing)'}` (`:157`). The `(nothing)` arm is unreachable: `execFileSync` throws first.
3. **The gate line is host-dependent, and the body does not say so.** "`npx vitest run` … **99 passed**" is
   reproducible here only because this laptop has `claude` at
   `~/.nvm/versions/node/v22.1.0/bin/claude`. On CI the same pair is 98 + 1 failed. The body's Gate section
   reports a local green over a red required check.

The fix is small and belongs in the guard, not the test: resolve inside a `try`, normalise not-found to `''`,
and let the existing `!== bin` comparison produce the guard's own message. That also makes the `(nothing)`
arm live.
